book_title: Chapter 9: Bull vs. Bear, Scenario Math & Our REJECTED Verdict
question: Weighing both sides and exact risk-reward math, what is our new-capital verdict, holding action, and cash plan?

epigraph.quote: The difference between patience and procrastination is simple: patience waits for a positive edge; procrastination hides behind a watch zone when the math already failed.
epigraph.author: Institutional Risk Committee Standard

web_blocks.title: Weighing the bull steelman against the bear steelman

web_blocks.html: Our Pass 1 audit assigned CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health. Pairing that with Pass 2 valuation ($48.89, 4.58% standalone 2027 FCF yield) and Stage 4 technicals demands an unhedged call [23, 24, 29, 38]. We steelman both sides honestly before letting arithmetic decide. The decisive test is whether any entry zone clears 1.50:1 reward-to-risk and beats the 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield [38, 39].

web_blocks.takeaway: Probability-weighted expected value is $48.37/share (-1.1% from $48.89), trailing the 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield. Both a Stage 2 reclaim ($53.25–$55.50) and Pivot S2 ($44.49, above $39.67 strip value) fail our 1.50:1 asymmetry floor [23, 38, 39].

web_blocks.title: Probability-weighted 12-month outcome scenarios and math proof

web_blocks.html: Our three-scenario matrix prices real cash claims and regulatory odds without optimism [29, 31, 38]. Weighting 30% Bear ($31.22), 45% Base ($50.00), and 25% Bull ($66.00) yields an expected value of $48.37 (-1.1% from $48.89) [23]. Under our anti-hedging standard, WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT requires an actionable entry zone clearing 1.50:1 reward-to-risk to Base fair value. Here, a Stage 2 reclaim ($53.25–$55.50) sits above our $50.00 Base Case (-9.9% return). Pivot S2 ($44.49 vs. $33.00 stop, or $31.22 Bear) also sits above $39.67 EIA strip value at 0.48:1 [23]. Only a below-strip washout into $36.00–$38.00 ($33.00 stop) paired with >$3.00/MMBtu gas, HSR clearance, PipeBox paydown, and Stage 1/2 reclaim could reset R:R, so we assign REJECTED (VALUATION, CASH_FLOW, TREND; TIER_0).

web_blocks.takeaway: Expected value ($48.37) implies -1.1% 12-month return against -36.1% Bear downside ($31.22). EQT fails valuation, cash-flow, and trend gates, requiring REJECTED instead of hedging with WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT [23, 38, 39].

web_blocks.title: Multi-horizon judgment, sizing screen, and capital redeployment

web_blocks.html: Across all three horizons, capital discipline favors holding zero shares and keeping cash in T-bills [23]. Short-term traders avoid Stage 4 Markdown beneath falling 50-day and 200-day averages [23]. Medium-term investors reject new capital because 4.58% to 5.13% normalized 2027 FCF yields lose to 5.04% Treasuries [38, 39]. Long-term investors note the CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL asset quality. Still, they should wait for PipeBox cash-sweep reduction, HSR clearance, and a Stage 2 base before re-underwriting [29, 36].

web_blocks.html: Re-Underwriting Triggers: Keep EQT on REJECTED (0% allocation) until one of two triggers occurs. First, 2027–2028 Henry Hub futures rally above $3.25/MMBtu alongside clean Range HSR clearance, PipeBox paydown, and a Stage 2 reclaim above $55.34 on ≥1.3x volume. Second, a below-strip washout into $36.00–$38.00 ($33.00 structural stop) paired with normalized 2027–2028 Henry Hub gas above $3.00/MMBtu (~$3.10+/MMBtu, lifting attributable FCF above $1.74B standalone / $2.38B pro forma for >7.5% FCF yield vs. 6.05%/6.78% at $2.88 strip), clean HSR clearance, PipeBox paydown, and a Stage 1/2 reclaim.

book_paragraphs: Now comes the moment of truth where every model, footnote, and chart bar gets distilled into one honest decision. Looking at EQT Corporation at $48.89 on November 20, 2026, our New-Capital Verdict is REJECTED—backed by three concrete failure classes: Valuation, Cash Flow, and Trend. Because you hold zero shares across Charles Schwab and Robinhood, your Current Holding Action is NOT_HELD, with zero shares to sell and 100% of marginal cash staying safely in short-term Treasury bills.

Let us walk through both sides of the aisle to be sure we are not missing a hidden bull turn. The Bull steelman is real: EQT operates at a ~$2.00 per MMBtu unlevered breakeven, cut total debt to $5.59 billion, delivered $5.19 billion in nine-month operating cash flow, and owns irreplaceable Appalachian midstream egress [5, 29]. Over the long run, rising U.S. LNG exports toward 19 Bcf/d in 2027 and AI data-center power demand could tighten domestic gas balances [22, 38].

Yet the Bear steelman wins the math on today's 12-month horizon. First, the EIA cut its 2027 Henry Hub forecast to $2.88 per MMBtu [38]. At $2.88 gas, Blackstone's 60% PipeBox cash sweep (~$450 million annualized while $3.3 billion Base Return remains) reduces standalone attributable free cash flow to ~$1.40 billion—just a 4.58% equity yield against a 5.04% risk-free 10-year Treasury [29, 39]. Second, EQT carries $13.2 billion in off-balance-sheet take-or-pay pipe commitments and 2027 three-way collars with sold $2.50 puts that expose downside if gas drops further [29, 30]. Third, the Range Resources merger faces federal HSR antitrust review carrying an asymmetric $1,148 million EQT break-up fee [31, 36].

Weighting our three 12-month scenarios—30% Bear at $31.22, 45% Base at $50.00, and 25% Bull at $66.00—gives an expected value of $48.37 per share, or -1.1% below today's $48.89 price. Calling that WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT would violate our anti-hedging discipline: a Stage 2 reclaim above $53.25 to $55.50 sits above our $50.00 Base Case fair value, and Pivot S2 ($44.49) sits above our $39.67 EIA strip valuation with just 0.48-to-1 reward-to-risk against a $33.00 structural stop (or 0.41-to-1 against $31.22 Bear). When neither momentum nor Pivot S2 clears 1.50-to-1, the only intellectually honest rating is REJECTED.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The hardest discipline in equity research is downgrading an elite operator when forward commodity math, senior cash sweeps, and a Stage 4 chart strip away your margin of safety. Never use 'wait for support' as an excuse when the math fails at support too.

book_subsections.title: Why Prior $64 Targets Were Too High—And What Would Reopen the File
paragraphs: It is worth pausing on why our November 13 dossier set a $64.00 Base Case target while today's fresh Pass 2 model lands at $50.00. The prior calculation assumed $3.25 per MMBtu gas, applied a 7.5x EV-to-EBITDA multiple, omitted Range Resources' ~$1.4 billion net debt from the enterprise bridge, and overlooked Blackstone's 60% PipeBox cash sweep. Stripping out confirmation bias and rebuilding from Q3 Form 10-Q Note 9 and the November 10 EIA strip dropped Base fair value by $14 per share [29, 38].

Still, an institutional desk never permanently ignores a tier-one asset base. Two clear triggers would bring EQT back onto our active bench: either a sustained rally in 2027–2028 Henry Hub strips above $3.25 per MMBtu combined with clean HSR clearance, PipeBox paydown, and a high-volume Stage 2 reclaim above $55.34, or a below-strip washout into $36.00–$38.00 ($33.00 structural stop) paired with normalized 2027–2028 Henry Hub gas above $3.00 per MMBtu (~$3.10+/MMBtu, generating $1.74B+ standalone / $2.38B+ pro forma attributable FCF for >7.5% yield, vs. 6.05%/6.78% at EIA's $2.88 strip), clean HSR clearance, PipeBox paydown, and Stage 1/2 base formation.

book_subsections.title: Exact Holding Check & 100%-Reconciled Capital Redeployment
paragraphs: Our November 20 positions ledger confirms zero EQT shares and zero EQT options across both Charles Schwab and Robinhood. That makes execution straightforward: no shares to sell, no forced tax event, and zero live stop orders to manage. Set two passive price-and-news alerts—one at $55.34 for a >$3.25/MMBtu Stage 2 reclaim check and one at $38.00 for a below-strip $36.00–$38.00 reset (requiring >$3.00/MMBtu gas, HSR clearance, PipeBox paydown, and Stage 1/2 reclaim)—and close the order ticket.

For your marginal cash unit, keep 100% in USD Cash or Treasury bills earning roughly 4.76% to 5.04% while the S&P 500 sits in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend [39]. We compared two Stage 2 alternatives from our live snapshot: shortlist leader Eli Lilly (LLY at $1,347.11, 0% now, offering 2.08-to-1 R:R only on a pullback into $1,282.61–$1,321.67) and outside LNG exporter Cheniere Energy (LNG at $294.84, 0%, yielding just 0.57-to-1 to $315.00). Neither justifies displacing cash today.

book_subsections.title: Position Sizing Discipline & Key Milestones Through 2027
paragraphs: Under our portfolio risk-unit governance, a REJECTED (Tier 0) rating locks recommended exposure at 0.0% of net worth. Notice how much risk that saves you: if Henry Hub dips below $2.50 per MMBtu and triggers losses on EQT's sold three-way collar puts while FTC/DOJ scrutiny drags out the Range merger, EQT could slide 36.1% toward our $31.22 Bear Case [29, 31].

Keep three dates on your radar over the coming quarters without tying up capital: weekly Thursday EIA storage draws, federal HSR second-request or clearance filings on the Range merger, and EQT's Q4 2026 guidance detailing 2027 PipeBox distributions and maintenance capital. Let the market prove the turn before risking a single dollar.

book_subsections.title: Final Underwriting Takeaway: Respect the Business, Respect Your Cash
paragraphs: Rejecting EQT at $48.89 does not mean dismissing the operational machine Toby Rice and Jeremy Knop built since 2019 [16]. Cutting debt below $5.6 billion and driving unlevered breakevens near $2.00 per MMBtu gives EQT real staying power across bad gas winters [5, 29].

Even great operators become poor investments when prior claims, equity dilution, and macro supply compress forward returns below Treasury yields. Until 2027–2028 gas strips recover above $3.25 per MMBtu with Range HSR clearance and a Stage 2 reclaim—or a below-strip flush into $36.00–$38.00 ($33.00 stop) coincides with >$3.00/MMBtu normalized gas, HSR clearance, PipeBox paydown, and Stage 1/2 confirmation—your best trade is earning 5% in T-bills.
